definition: The country where an imported article was manufactured, produced or grown. Work done in a second country changes the origin only if it substantially transforms the article.
Further work or added material in another country that is significant enough to make that country the new country of origin.
Generally the last person in the United States who receives the article in the form in which it was imported; for goods sold at retail in imported form, the retail buyer.
An additional duty of 10 percent of the final appraised value on an article not legally marked with its country of origin at importation, unless it is exported or destroyed under customs supervision.
The list in 19 CFR 134.33 of articles excepted from individual country-of-origin marking, such as buttons, eggs, firewood and monuments.
The price actually paid or payable for merchandise when sold for exportation to the United States, plus specified additions; the first basis US Customs uses to appraise imports.
The total payment for the imported merchandise, whether made directly or indirectly.
An item supplied to the producer directly or indirectly, free of charge or at reduced cost, for use in producing the imported goods — for example tools, dies and molds.
An order that instructs Customs to assess antidumping duties on the merchandise it covers; importers must make a cash deposit of estimated duties.
A ruling on whether a particular product is covered by an antidumping or countervailing duty order; while a scope inquiry runs, entries already suspended stay suspended.
The calendar month in which the anniversary of the publication of an AD/CVD order or suspension of investigation falls; reviews may be requested during that month.
Amazon's fee on each item sold: a percentage of the total price or a per-item minimum, whichever is greater.
eBay's percentage fee on the total amount of a sale — in most categories 13.6% up to $7,500 per item — where the total includes item price, handling, shipping and sales tax.
An order placed from the shop within 30 days of a buyer clicking an Etsy Offsite Ad. Etsy charges the Offsite Ads fee only when its advertising directly results in a sale.
